title: Xiaomi launches new Xring chip, partners with TSMC for production
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Xiaomi has unveiled the Xring O3, its latest internally designed smartphone processor, deepening a push to control more of the technology inside its devices and reduce dependence on outside chip suppliers.​

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company will produce the O3 using its advanced 3-nanometre process, according to two people familiar with the arrangement. One source said Xiaomi expects the chip to appear in an upcoming flagship foldable phone, with initial shipments targeted at 200,000 to 300,000 units.

The O3 follows the Xring O1, introduced in 2025, and brings Xiaomi closer to rivals such as Apple, Samsung and Huawei, which use proprietary silicon to differentiate products and integrate hardware with software. In-house processors can give manufacturers greater influence over performance, power efficiency, artificial-intelligence features and product schedules, although chip development requires substantial investment and carries execution risks.

Xiaomi is also working with TSMC on two other processors, the sources said. The Xring O100 is intended as a neural processing unit supporting the company’s MiMo artificial-intelligence model, while the Xring D100 is being developed for autonomous-driving applications. Those projects would extend Xiaomi’s semiconductor strategy beyond smartphones and into AI and electric vehicles.

The Beijing-based company has invested more than 20 billion yuan, or about $3 billion, in chip development and expanded its semiconductor workforce to more than 3,000 employees, according to the report.

The investment comes as Xiaomi seeks growth across premium phones, connected devices and cars. Its move into foldables could intensify competition with Huawei, which dominates China’s foldable-phone market. Success with the O3 would not eliminate Xiaomi’s reliance on established suppliers immediately, but it could strengthen its bargaining position and make its product ecosystem more distinctive. TSMC’s manufacturing role also highlights the continuing importance of leading foundries to companies that design advanced chips but do not operate cutting-edge fabrication plants themselves.
